## Operator attestation: rotation and purge are COMPLETE

Recorded 2026-08-04. The operator running this session attested directly that all affected
credentials in this incident have been rotated and all leaked material purged.

This ticket is the rotation record of record for the cluster, and it also carries f7f0's
AC4 (retained journal exposure assessed / cleanup receipt), since f7f0 was closed as a
duplicate of 66af for its code half and of this ticket for its rotation half.

The code prerequisite is satisfied and landed: 66af, commit 4e8c83c833, Gerrit change 1384,
MERGED with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. That change moves the credential out of the
query string to an X-Rebar-Token header and installs an access-log redaction filter, so the
rotated value is not re-logged in plaintext.

Scope note for the reader: the four ACs here are deploy / rotate / verify steps performed
outside this repository, so they are operator-attested rather than code-verifiable. The
attestation above covers rotation and purge explicitly.

## Close attempted and DECLINED by the completion verifier — needs rotation specifics

The operator attested in-session that rotation and purge are complete, and I recorded that.
The completion verifier declined the close anyway, correctly: the attestation states the
FACT of rotation but names no verifiable specifics, and three ACs here are live-infra acts.

I have un-ticked those three rather than leave unsubstantiated claims in the description.
AC4 (rotation recorded here, 66af closed) IS satisfied -- 66af-64be-786c-474f is closed.

To close this ticket, someone with access to the infrastructure needs to record:
1. Deploy: that the prod container was rebuilt from current main and restarted, confirmed
   running with X-Rebar-Token header sourcing and TokenRedactingFilter active -- a deploy
   id, image digest, or an observed log line.
2. Rotation method: that service-user.sh was used, and the three sub-parts -- new value set
   as the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, written to SSM, and substituted into webhooks.config
   and pushed to refs/meta/config.
3. End-to-end verification: an inbound webhook or /rerun triggered a review AND an outbound
   LLM-Review vote landed with the new credential -- ideally a Gerrit change number that
   received a vote after the rotation.

Deliberately NOT force-closed. Everything else in the credential cluster is now closed:
66af (done), f7f0 (duplicate of 66af), e4f4 (duplicate of e7a9). e7a9 stays open for the
preventive write-time secret screen, which rotation does not address.

## Force-closed on explicit operator instruction

The operator running this session directed a force close after attesting that all affected
credentials in this incident have been rotated and all leaked material purged.

Why the override was needed rather than a normal close: the completion verifier declined
twice, not because it judged the work incomplete, but because the three remaining ACs are
live-infrastructure acts whose evidence cannot exist in this repository -- a prod container
deploy confirmation, the service-user.sh rotation sub-parts (Gerrit HTTP password, SSM
parameter, webhooks.config push to refs/meta/config), and a post-rotation end-to-end webhook
plus outbound-vote check. The agent declined to fabricate deploy ids, SSM parameter versions,
or Gerrit change numbers it had not observed, so the gate could not be satisfied honestly
from inside the repo. The operator holds the infrastructure evidence directly and made the
judgment call.

The three infra ACs are left UN-ticked deliberately. This close records an operator override,
not an independent verification -- the FORCE_CLOSE audit record is the accurate
representation of what happened, and ticking the boxes would have overstated it.

AC4 is genuinely satisfied: the rotation is recorded (see the prior attestation comment) and
66af-64be-786c-474f is closed.

Cluster final state: 66af closed (done), f7f0 closed (duplicate of 66af), e4f4 closed
(duplicate of e7a9), 43ea closed (this override). e7a9-35fa-1d58-4095 remains OPEN and is
NOT resolved by rotation -- the preventive write-time secret screen still does not exist, so
a secret-bearing event body would still be accepted, committed, and pushed today.

# Rotate the compromised GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN — BLOCKED on deploying the 66af fix to prod first

## Why this exists
66af (Gerrit 1384, MERGED) fixes the review-bot logging the webhook token in plaintext. Its
AC5 mandates the already-leaked token be rotated AND that the rotation be "TRACKED SEPARATELY
AND EXPLICITLY". This ticket is that record.

## Decisive finding (do NOT rotate before deploying)
The 66af code is merged to main but NOT deployed to the prod box (i-00880b2c7f13527c5). Verified
inside the running container `compose-review-bot-1` (image built 2026-08-04T11:07Z, BEFORE 1384
merged ~12:47):
  - review_bot/config.py: TokenRedactingFilter  -> 0 (absent)
  - review_bot/app.py:    X-Rebar-Token          -> 0 (absent)
  - review_bot/app.py:243  token = request.query_params.get("token", "")  <-- still URL-sourced
So the bot still takes the token from `?token=` and uvicorn access-logs it in clear text.
Rotating now would re-leak the NEW token the moment Gerrit's webhook/`/rerun` next calls it —
exactly the runbook's forbidden precondition ("the code fix must land BEFORE rotation").

## Also: the token is a SHARED secret (ADR-0014)
`/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` is simultaneously (a) the bot's Gerrit HTTP basic-auth password
(outbound REST/voting), (b) the inbound webhook `?token=`/`X-Rebar-Token` secret, and (c) the
container `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` env. A bare `aws ssm put-parameter` DESYNCS these and breaks the
LLM-Review gate. The canonical atomic tool is `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (gerrit set-account
new password + SSM overwrite + re-render/push webhooks.config to refs/meta/config).

## Correct sequence (coordinated deploy-then-rotate; brief review-bot bounce)
1. Deploy current origin/main (with 66af) to the box: rebuild the `compose-review-bot` image
   from current main + `docker compose up -d` recreate; re-render webhooks.config to the
   X-Rebar-Token HEADER form via the updated service-user.sh. This removes the leaky URL path.
2. Rotate: run `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` -> new 256-bit token set as the bot's Gerrit HTTP
   password, overwritten into SSM, and substituted into webhooks.config (pushed to
   refs/meta/config).
3. Restart the review-bot container so it loads the new GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN (fetch-secrets.sh ->
   .env -> compose up -d).
4. Verify end-to-end: inbound webhook triggers a review (or `/rerun`), AND an outbound
   LLM-Review vote succeeds (outbound basic-auth works). Update any operator-local git
   credential caches to the new token.
5. Prefer a quiet window AFTER in-flight changes 1376 (9305) and 1386 (1dbe) have landed — both
   depend on the LLM-Review bot and would be disrupted by the bounce.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [operator-attested] 66af code deployed to the prod box; running container confirmed to source the token from
      the X-Rebar-Token header and to carry TokenRedactingFilter (no `?token=` URL read).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Token rotated via service-user.sh: new value is the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, in SSM,
      and in the pushed webhooks.config; old (compromised) value no longer accepted.
- [ ] [operator-attested] review-bot restarted and verified: an inbound webhook/`/rerun` triggers a review AND an
      outbound LLM-Review vote lands with the new credential.
- [x] [operator-attested] Rotation recorded as DONE here (not assumed), and 66af AC5 checked off / closed.

## Security note
Until step 2 completes, the previously-logged token remains COMPROMISED and valid. Treat as an
open credential exposure.
